summary: The run had adequate offensive output but suffered from severe HP attrition before and throughout Act 2. Several optional-risk choices and the Coffee Dripper plan left HP as a finite resource, culminating in the Collector fight at only 23 HP and a final logged 15 HP while the boss remained at 245 HP. The main improvement is to reduce avoidable damage and make defensive or healing-oriented choices earlier, rather than relying on late combat damage to compensate.

lessons.title: Avoid avoidable HP and curse costs when already under pressure
lessons.situation: When an event offers healing or maximum HP alongside a curse/relic option, especially before a difficult Act 1 route or when using a no-rest boss relic.
lessons.lesson: Prefer the safe healing or max-HP option unless the alternative provides a clearly necessary payoff. Do not repeatedly spend HP on optional events when later recovery is limited.
evidence_points: At Act 1 Floor 3 with 80/80 HP, the run chose the box, gaining Regret, despite alternatives to heal 26 HP or gain 5 max HP.
At Act 1 Floor 10, 75 gold was spent removing Regret, and the run later took the Book event in Act 2 at 66 HP, losing another 10 HP.
lessons.reasoning: The first event created a curse that had to be removed at a shop, while the later event directly sacrificed HP. These costs were especially harmful because the run eventually selected Coffee Dripper and had no normal rest healing.

lessons.title: Treat Coffee Dripper as a commitment to damage avoidance
lessons.situation: After taking Coffee Dripper, whenever choosing between greedy upgrades, risky events, and defensive preparation while HP is falling.
lessons.lesson: With Coffee Dripper, preserve HP aggressively: prioritize safer fights, defensive cards, and avoiding optional self-damage. Do not assume future campfires will repair accumulated combat losses.
evidence_points: The run selected Coffee Dripper as its Act 1 boss relic, removing normal rest healing for the rest of the run.
Act 2 HP declined from 87 after the boss to 72, 54, 41, 37, 31, and 23 by Floor 32, while the run used Peace Pipe at both logged rest decisions instead of receiving healing.
The Collector fight began at 23/87 HP and the last logged state was 15/87 HP.
lessons.reasoning: The trajectory shows sustained HP attrition with no reliable recovery mechanism. Once Coffee Dripper was chosen, every avoidable hit and HP payment permanently reduced the margin for the Act 2 boss.

lessons.title: Skip redundant rewards when the deck already has enough damage
lessons.situation: When a reward offers another mediocre attack or duplicate utility card and the permanent deck is already large or contains multiple copies of that role.
lessons.lesson: Use skip more often to keep the deck focused. Prefer cards that solve the current survival problem, and avoid adding redundant attacks merely because they are playable.
evidence_points: The final 28-card deck contains two Headbutts, two Angers, two upgraded Shrug It Offs plus one unupgraded Shrug It Off, and multiple other attacks.
The run repeatedly accepted additional attacks or duplicates, including Headbutt at Act 1 Floors 5 and 7, Anger at Floor 6, and Hemokinesis at Act 2 Floor 31.
At Act 2 Floor 25, the run did skip a reward, showing that skipping was available, but it continued adding True Grit and Hemokinesis afterward.
lessons.reasoning: The final build had substantial attack density and some defensive tools, but remained vulnerable to HP loss. More selective rewards would improve draw quality and increase the chance of drawing defensive or scaling cards when needed.
